verses.text: “If you will return, Israel,” says Yahweh, “if you will return to me, and if you will put away your abominations out of my sight; then you shall not be removed;
and you shall swear, ‘As Yahweh lives,’ in truth, in justice, and in righteousness. The nations shall bless themselves in him, and in him shall they glory.”
For Yahweh says to the men of Judah and to Jerusalem, “Break up your fallow ground, and don’t sow among thorns.

Circumcise yourselves to Yahweh, and take away the foreskins of your heart, you men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem; lest my wrath go out like fire, and burn so that no one can quench it, because of the evil of your doings.
Declare in Judah, and publish in Jerusalem; and say, ‘Blow the trumpet in the land!’ Cry aloud and say, ‘Assemble yourselves! Let us go into the fortified cities!’
Set up a standard toward Zion. Flee for safety! Don’t wait; for I will bring evil from the north, and a great destruction.”
A lion has gone up from his thicket, and a destroyer of nations; he is on his way, he has gone out from his place, to make your land desolate, that your cities be laid waste, without inhabitant.
For this clothe yourself with sackcloth, lament and wail; for the fierce anger of Yahweh hasn’t turned back from us.
“It shall happen at that day,” says Yahweh, “that the heart of the king shall perish, and the heart of the princes; and the priests shall be astonished, and the prophets shall wonder.”
Then I said, “Ah, Lord Yahweh! Surely you have greatly deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, ‘You shall have peace;’ whereas the sword reaches to the heart.”
At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem, “A hot wind from the bare heights in the wilderness toward the daughter of my people, not to winnow, nor to cleanse;
a full wind from these shall come for me. Now I will also utter judgments against them.”
Behold, he shall come up as clouds, and his chariots shall be as the whirlwind: his horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us! For we are ruined.
Jerusalem, wash your heart from wickedness, that you may be saved. How long shall your evil thoughts lodge within you?
For a voice declares from Dan, and publishes evil from the hills of Ephraim:
“Tell the nations; behold, publish against Jerusalem, ‘Watchers come from a far country, and raise their voice against the cities of Judah.
As keepers of a field, they are against her all around, because she has been rebellious against me,’” says Yahweh.
“Your way and your doings have brought these things to you. This is your wickedness; for it is bitter, for it reaches to your heart.”
My anguish, my anguish! I am pained at my very heart; my heart is disquieted in me; I can’t hold my peace; because you have heard, O my soul, the sound of the trumpet, the alarm of war.
Destruction on destruction is cried; for the whole land is laid waste: suddenly are my tents destroyed, and my curtains in a moment.
How long shall I see the standard, and hear the sound of the trumpet?
“For my people are foolish, they don’t know me. They are foolish children, and they have no understanding. They are skillful in doing evil, but to do good they have no knowledge.”
I saw the earth, and, behold, it was waste and void; and the heavens, and they had no light.
I saw the mountains, and behold, they trembled, and all the hills moved back and forth.
I saw, and behold, there was no man, and all the birds of the sky had fled.
I saw, and behold, the fruitful field was a wilderness, and all its cities were broken down at the presence of Yahweh, before his fierce anger.
For Yahweh says, “The whole land shall be a desolation; yet will I not make a full end.
For this the earth will mourn, and the heavens above be black; because I have spoken it, I have purposed it, and I have not repented, neither will I turn back from it.”
Every city flees for the noise of the horsemen and archers; they go into the thickets, and climb up on the rocks: every city is forsaken, and not a man dwells therein.

You, when you are made desolate, what will you do? Though you clothe yourself with scarlet, though you deck yourself with ornaments of gold, though you enlarge your eyes with makeup, you make yourself beautiful in vain. Your lovers despise you. They seek your life.

For I have heard a voice as of a woman in travail, the anguish as of her who gives birth to her first child, the voice of the daughter of Zion, who gasps for breath, who spreads her hands, saying, “Woe is me now! For my soul faints before the murderers.”

footnotes.content: The Lord opens with invitation, not condemnation. 'If you will return'—notice the gentleness in the condition. He isn't saying 'you cannot,' but 'come home.' Putting away what defiles us is the first movement toward His presence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An oath 'As Yahweh lives' spoken in truth, justice, and righteousness—these aren't three separate things, but one commitment to align ourselves completely with Him. When we're right with God, others see His character in us and are drawn to His goodness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Break up your fallow ground'—a farmer's image, speaking to ancient Judah who knew the soil. Hard ground won't receive seed. Yahweh isn't asking for perfection, but for us to stop resisting His work in our hearts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Circumcise yourselves to Yahweh'—He's calling for inward transformation, not outward ritual. The real cutting away is of pride, self-will, the hardness that keeps us from Him. Without this inner change, His wrath burns like unquenched fire.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The alarm is real—'Blow the trumpet' in Judah, publish in Jerusalem. When danger comes, we scatter toward what we think will save us. But the trumpet that matters most calls us to gather into the stronghold of God's presence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zion stands as a beacon—the city of God's dwelling. To 'set up a standard' there is to look toward where God reigns, to remember He is still present even in the hour of threat.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The lion—fierce, unstoppable, emerging from cover. Jeremiah sees the invader coming from the north as an instrument of judgment. When we abandon the God who shields us, no wall holds forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sackcloth, lamentation, wailing—the prophetic call isn't to despair, but to grieve what has been lost by turning away. This is the honest anguish that precedes the healing that comes through turning back to God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kings, princes, priests, prophets—all lose their bearings when judgment comes. The structures we build for ourselves crumble. Only those anchored to the Lord find steadiness when the world shakes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah himself cries out in honest bewilderment—'You have greatly deceived this people, saying You shall have peace.' He speaks the ache of watching people trust false shepherds who promise what only God can give.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The 'hot wind from the bare heights'—a desert wind that doesn't winnow or cleanse, but destroys. In that arid land, such winds were harbingers of devastation. Judgment comes, not to refine, but to lay waste.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh's judgments are not arbitrary but answer to rebellion. He has spoken—and His word holds. There's a terrible clarity here: what we have chosen to sow, we shall reap.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Clouds, whirlwind, horses swifter than eagles—the image of overwhelming, unstoppable force. The invader comes like God Himself, reminding us that human power is as grass before Him who truly commands the heavens.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Wash your heart from wickedness'—Jerusalem herself is called to cleanse. There's still grace here, still an opening. The heart lodging evil thoughts is the true disease; the city's fall is secondary.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dan and Ephraim—northern strongholds. When 'watchers' cry from there, they signal that the north is already compromised. For Jeremiah's hearers, this would have meant the threat was imminent, drawing closer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The nations are called to witness Jerusalem's fall, to publish her shame. When we turn from God, our witness becomes our weakness; others see not His glory, but the ruin of His defiant people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Like keepers of a field, they are against her all around'—a siege, a strangling. Rebellion has left Judah exposed on every side. There is no escape except through the gate of repentance, which closes with each refusal.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Your way and your doings have brought these things to you.' There's no room for blame-shifting here. Yahweh makes clear the connection between choice and consequence, between the heart's direction and its fruit.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah's own anguish—'My anguish, my anguish!'—shows the cost of knowing and speaking truth. His heart is torn, not by hate for Judah, but by love and grief at what she has chosen. This is the prophet's burden.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Destruction on destruction'—the accumulation of loss. Suddenly, tents are destroyed, curtains torn away. What took generations to build crumbles in a moment when the foundations are laid on anything but God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'How long shall I see the standard, and hear the sound of the trumpet?' Even Jeremiah, the faithful messenger, is worn by the prolonged alarm. The watchman's vigil takes its toll on the watcher's soul.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'They are foolish children, and they have no understanding'—and here's the tragic flip: 'skillful in doing evil, but to do good they have no knowledge.' It's not ignorance of God, but deliberate blindness to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jeremiah sees the land 'waste and void'—echoing Genesis where the earth was formless before creation. In vision, he sees judgment unmaking order itself. When God withdraws His sustaining presence, chaos returns.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mountains trembling, hills moving back and forth—the very pillars of stability become unstable. In apocalyptic vision, Jeremiah shows what occurs when the God who holds all things shakes what is built on rebellion.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'No man, and all the birds of the sky had fled'—emptiness, abandonment. Life itself flees when God's judgment falls. This is the end of busyness and noise; only desolation remains.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The fruitful field becomes wilderness, cities broken down—all that humans labored to build crumbles before Yahweh's presence and anger. Our works are secure only when built with Him, not against Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Yet will I not make a full end'—even here, in the deepest judgment, grace breaks through. Desolation is not permanent; the covenant God has not abandoned His people entirely. There remains a future for those who turn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Earth mourns, heavens are black—creation itself grieves. Yahweh has spoken, purposed it, and will not turn back. His Word stands; what is decreed unfolds. We cannot negotiate with the reality of His judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every city flees, all forsaken—the panic is total. Where once were communities and commerce, only abandoned ruins. The judgment is not selective; it sweeps the land clean of those who would not turn.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jerusalem dressing in scarlet and gold, enlarging eyes with makeup—she tries to seduce her lovers in the hour of her desolation, but they despise her and seek to destroy. When trust is placed anywhere but in God, betrayal follows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The daughter of Zion—Jerusalem herself—cries out in travail and gasps for breath. Readers today hear an echo in that ancient anguish: the soul's desperate cry when we have run from home and find ourselves undone. But even in that moment, she can turn back to her Father.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
